title: Shabla Lighthouse
visualBrief: Tall red and white tapering octagon with real recessed narrow openings, crisp corner ribs and a small dark lantern. Broad square striped masonry base with stacked southern windows and attached low hipped keeper house to the north.

sourceFacts.basis: Municipal32m height, embedded tower coordinate and inspected official/July2026 photographs. The mapped attached service house lies south of the municipal tower control. The exact-QID node18.3m south is retained for identity only. Tower cross-section and floor allocation are photo proportions.

geographicProposal.notes: +Y up; +Z points roughly north (2.71 degrees true), the stacked tower openings face north, the attached keeper house extends south (-Z), and +X door/steps face inland/west. Municipal tower coordinates and mapped house axis choose the sign; the exact-QID OSM node is an identity control with an approximately18.3m southward position discrepancy. Municipal embedded tower coordinates are the position control, not an engineering survey. The exact-QID OSM node lies about18.3m south, and its identity alone does not validate its point position. North-up aerial and the inspected July2026 west-side photograph establish house/tower quadrant; photo metadata azimuth312 disagrees with the GPS-to-tower direction and is not used as a bearing. House centering follows the mapped rectangle; its scale, 8.5m square tower base, taper, windows, floor allocation, rail spacing and fittings remain photo proportions. Towerheight32m is distinct from focalheight36m; Y0 uses host terrain contact, not surveyed sea level. Detached station buildings, hedges, shore and interiors are not part of this asset. Paint age and individual masonry are generalized.

limitations: The modeled exterior follows the cited published facts and inspected photographs. Unpublished dimensions and local fittings are explicitly photo-proportioned; no claim of engineering survey accuracy is made.
Portable PBR and shared metric surfaces are provided. Surface weathering, material color under local lighting and fine facade relief require close render review before maximum-detail acceptance.

Paint wear and individual repairs are represented by shared masonry; the official image has no precise capture date. Tower plan is photograph-scaled against32m height; neighboring detached station houses remain separate map features.
referenceRights: Original geometry and shared procedural materials. Official photographs are research references only; no reference imagery or third-party mesh is embedded or redistributed.
